_about: How the dangling DNS lens reads stored records for ones that point at something the subject may no longer hold. A name's alias chain is followed as dns.json says. claimable_services are hosted services whose resource names anyone can claim once the owner deletes the resource, so an alias to a name on one with no stored address is the classic subdomain takeover: each has the patterns (regular expressions over the alias target) that name its resources and a source documenting the risk. delegation_labels are the relations that delegate a domain to name servers besides NS records (a registration record's name servers). A domain whose stored registration record has an expiry field from expiry_fields in the past can be registered by anyone; within expiry_warning_days it is reported as expiring. An address record not seen again within stale_record_days of the last time its name was seen may point at an address since released. Findings are leads to verify with a live lookup, not proof. Add values here, not in Go code.
